title: The Top 100 Gen AI Consumer Apps — 7th Edition | Andreessen Horowitz
gist: a16z's 7th Top 100 consumer AI ranking adds YipitData card-spend data: consumer AI is wide but shallow (4.5% of US consumers pay for ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude), spend follows a power law, and the next leg depends on personal agents and non-subscription business models.

insights.claim: Nearly half of US consumers report using AI but only 25% use it daily, and by August just 4.5% had an active paid personal subscription to ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude (up from 2.1% a year earlier).
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Paid consumer AI penetration is still tiny; headroom depends on new products and business models.
insights.locator: The biggest takeaway from this new data

insights.claim: Only 13% of consumers who pay for one AI product pay for even one other AI tool, so consumer AI subscriptions are largely single-vendor.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Winner-take-most dynamics per payer; cross-subscription is limited.

insights.claim: Only 8% of US ChatGPT subscribers also subscribe to Claude, suggesting the two products serve largely distinct user bases.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Competition between labs is less zero-sum than traffic rank implies.

themes.theme: AI spend follows a power law

insights.claim: The top 1% of AI payers account for 19.5% of observed US consumer AI spend, more than the bottom 50% combined (16.6%), and the top 10% account for roughly half of all spending.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Consumer AI revenue is a prosumer/power-user market; monetization quality beats user counts.

insights.claim: The top 1% of payers spend an average of $903 per month on AI via consumer cards, up 80% in 18 months, versus a median payer at about $25 per month that has barely grown spend.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Growth in spend is coming from intensifying power users, not broadening of the base.

insights.claim: Top spenders disproportionately buy automation and building tools (n8n, fal, Manus, Nous Research Hermes Agent) and creative tools (Higgsfield, Figma, HeyGen).
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Spend leaders are agent/automation and creative vendors, many absent from traffic lists.

insights.claim: 29 of the top 50 AI vendors by US consumer spend do not appear on any web or mobile traffic list, and only seven companies make all three lists, with ChatGPT first on each.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Traffic-based rankings miss where the money is; track spend panels for vendor selection.

insights.claim: ChatGPT leads Gemini roughly 2x and Claude 6x in August web visits, and has 3x more US consumer paid subscribers than Claude or Gemini.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: OpenAI retains consumer scale leadership.

insights.claim: Claude has become the clear #3 consumer AI product, passing DeepSeek and Perplexity in traffic and passing Gemini on US consumer subscribers earlier this year, helped by Cowork, Claude Design, Fable 5 and a #1 free US mobile app ranking during Anthropic's Pentagon dispute.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Anthropic's consumer share rose fast but from a small base.

insights.claim: Claude has 7.3% of its consumer payers on the $100+/month Max plan versus 1.3% for Google and 1.1% for ChatGPT on equivalent tiers, showing unusually aggressive monetization of power users with no ads.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Anthropic's ARPU mix is skewed premium; sensitive to power-user churn.

insights.claim: By mid-summer Claude's momentum faded: YipitData showed declining average daily sessions in July and August, slowing gross additions and rising churn, while ChatGPT re-accelerated with the July GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna launch and ChatGPT Work.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Consumer share gains are not locked in; watch churn data.

insights.claim: Anthropic, Google and OpenAI shipped 127 launches in six months with different targets: Anthropic prosumer, Google creative models, OpenAI both consumer and enterprise.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Each lab is pursuing a different audience, so 'who is winning' depends on the segment.

insights.claim: Personal agents have moved from developer-only to consumer reach within six months: Instinct, Tomo, Poke, Lindy and Town report hundreds of thousands of users, and incumbents responded with Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots and xAI's Grok Bot.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: A new consumer category with incumbents entering early.

insights.claim: Instinct's founder says 40% of users connect a personal credit card within three weeks, spend about $1,300 a month through it, and over $1 billion of annualized transaction volume flows through it, half in travel.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Founder-reported figures; indicates agents can be transaction rails, unverified.

insights.claim: Meta's Muse reportedly reached 250,000 daily actives in its first week and 5M downloads in under a month, but still trails Threads' 15M downloads in 22 days.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Early traction is real but below Meta's past launches.

insights.claim: Platforms are choosing sides on agent access: Amazon blocked Meta's Muse in under two weeks while Shopify, Instacart, OpenTable, Expedia, Ticketmaster and Plaid signed official integrations.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Agent access to commerce platforms is becoming a strategic battleground; integrators gain.

themes.theme: Where startups still win vs incumbents

insights.claim: Startups holding durable attention tend to own a differentiated model (Suno #7 on spend, ElevenLabs #10), a multi-model experience (Cursor, OpenRouter, Lovable, Replit), a specific audience (OpenEvidence for physicians, Venice for privacy) or a new interface that legacy products cannot adopt (Plaud hardware).
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: A checklist for judging whether a consumer AI startup is defensible against labs and incumbents.

insights.claim: Incumbents with embedded AI now rank high: Canva and Notion are top ten on web, Figma top 15, Superhuman debuted at #4 on spend, and Google has five web entries.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Distribution incumbents are capturing AI usage.

insights.claim: Excluded NSFW AI products would have made up more than 20% of the web traffic list, and OpenAI indefinitely paused its Adult Mode plans, leaving that demand to others.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Content-policy gaps create sizable niches for non-lab products.

insights.claim: Among 44 AI-native products on the web ranking, 84% offer subscriptions, 64% usage charges or credits, 14% ads and only 2% transaction fees, an inversion of the ad-funded consumer internet.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Ads and transaction revenue are the untapped AI consumer models.

insights.claim: OpenAI said ChatGPT advertising reached a $1 billion annualized run rate in August on 1.2 billion weekly active users, and OpenEvidence, used by an estimated 50-60% of US physicians, now partially monetizes via ads.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Ads are starting to scale in AI; ARPU is low relative to the user base.

insights.claim: Personal agents may monetize on affiliate fees or take rates rather than seats; Instinct and Muse plan transaction fees eventually but neither charges yet, and ChatGPT does not charge for purchases started in-product.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Watch for take-rate announcements as the next AI revenue stream.

insights.claim: AI companies relied on subscriptions because ads and transactions need scale and high model costs prevented burning for density; cheaper open-source models and task routing to cheaper models should ease this.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore
insights.so_what: Falling inference costs unlock ad-supported tiers.
